text:
Skip the hotel breakfast once in Osaka, and eat where the chefs shop instead. 🐟

Kizu Wholesale Market has been trading for more than 300 years. Restaurant chefs come for fish, vegetables and dried goods, and visitors can walk in and buy too. It's quieter and less polished than the famous markets, which is exactly why we like it.

How we'd do it:
🚇 Osaka Metro to Daikokucho, Exit 1, then about 3 minutes on foot
⏰ Arrive between 8:30 and 10:30. Stalls open around dawn and many close by late morning
📅 Closed Sundays and holidays, some Wednesdays and 31 Dec–4 Jan, so check the calendar on kizu-ichiba.com first

Order a seafood bowl, then head back into the city with the whole day still ahead of you.

Two more local markets, and the best time for each, in our guide 👉 https://japanbystation.com/osaka-local-markets

Would you trade a hotel breakfast for this? 👇
